chapter: This Is Your Life and film work
title: Being the subject of This Is Your Life
summary: She says she was the subject of This Is Your Life in about 1951 and recalls always going home for Christmas.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Also, another thing that I want to touch on a little bit is the -- I think this happened in '51. I was a subject on "This is Your Life."
Oh, I missed it. Tell me.

Yes, I was a subject on that, and I think -- I don't know, my memory might not serve me too well -- I think I was one of the first -- one of the first artists to do the thing live, you know, to do it direct. Because it was -- what do you call it, kinescope? The kinescope process that they followed. So I think my show was the first one to be

done live, and anyway, I was -- I was so surprised. I was completely -- there are some people that still remember this, as long ago as that has been, and I still have the film of it. It's kind of -- some of it's a little worn. I have to see if I can have it processed and --
Oh, yeah, you should have it restored.
And restored. I must keep that, you know.

But this was a marvelous thing, and I used to sit, you know, whenever I could and watch the different subjects on the show. And Ralph Edwards, who is a wonderful man, and such a personable man, and he -- he had -- isn't that funny, what is the guy's name? I can't even think of his name now. But was instrumental in really getting me on the show, and he had a girl working for him, and this girl, she was a maid, and the girl was a friend of mine, and she was instrumental in getting me, you know, getting me on the show. I say she was instrumental in getting me on the show because she found -- he found out that this girl was a friend of mine, and he had my records. Pascal, Al Pascal, that was the man's name. Al Pascal.

He was instrumental in getting me on the show, you know. He wanted me -- but I of course didn't know that. I wasn't supposed to know that I was going to be the subject of the show. And I was told that I was going to do -- what is the woman's name? Oh, dear, used to be a dancer. She was a marvelous

dancer. I was told that they were going to do her life, and it was on a New years Eve night, and what I used to do, I used to always get home for Christmas, you know. I wouldn't be away from home. I didn't -- I was home one time, away from my son at Christmastime, once, and I was never so miserable in my entire life. I was never so miserable, and I promised myself that I would never do that again, regardless of how much money, you know, it meant I would miss. I must spend Christmas, because I was used to this, you know, and coming from a large family Christmas always meant so much to me and my family. We always just loved Christmas. It was the big thing with us, even in Louisiana, you know, we just loved Christmas, and to have been away from home at Christmastime just really tore me up. So I promised I would always be.

But anyway, they contacted me, Mr. Pascal, and said they wanted me to be -- to do a number on this show, and it was going to be on a New Years Eve night. Well, on New Years Eve night some friends of mine were having a party or something, and you know, this was already arranged, for me to go to this party. I was looking forward to it, because working all the time you just didn't get a chance to do other things, you know, and I said, well, I'm going to be home, and I looked forward to going to this party.
